{"consolidated_memory":"NaN Feature in ml/features/encoder.py — Four Separate Incidents (2026-01-31 to 2026-08-01)

RECURRING PATTERN: All four incidents manifested as NaN values appearing in a single output column when encoding batches holding sparse columns, all in the ml pipeline's ml/features/encoder.py file. Each had a distinct trigger and root cause.

INCIDENT 1 [2026-01-31]
- Trigger: Deeply nested inputs beyond six levels
- Root Cause: Missing Unicode normalisation before hashing
- Fix: Normalised to NFC ahead of the digest
- PR #1619 / branch fix/nan-feature-1
- Result: Job completion time improved from 6 hours to 7 minutes

INCIDENT 2 [2026-03-16]
- Trigger: Payloads above roughly two megabytes
- Root Cause: Connection pool exhaustion under burst load
- Fix: Raised the pool ceiling and put a bounded wait queue in front of it
- PR #2268 / branch fix/nan-feature-2
- Stack: Python
- Test Coverage: tests/ml/test_encoder.py
- Result: Alert stayed quiet for 59 consecutive days

INCIDENT 3 [2026-04-05]
- Trigger: Traffic arriving through the corporate proxy
- Root Cause: Off-by-one in the slice bound
- Fix: Corrected the bound and added a property test around it
- PR #2515 / branch fix/nan-feature-3
- Result: Cold start performance improved 56%, dropping to 980 ms

INCIDENT 4 [2026-08-01]
- Trigger: Input list came in empty
- Root Cause: Unbounded retry loop with no backoff
- Fix: Capped the attempts and added exponential backoff with jitter
- PR #5195 / branch fix/nan-feature-4
- Result: p99 latency fell from 3.8 s to 90 ms

All incidents shared the same error signal (NaN in output column) and repro method (encode the batch holding sparse column), but required four separate fixes applied in sequence."}
